standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness of a module can be checked on a finite cover by principal open sets
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-cover}, cited at proof lines 16421 and 16431
standard_prerequisites.use: Turn finiteness of the localised cohomology modules into finiteness over the ring, and vanish the cohomology above the top degree.

standard_prerequisites.name: The m-pseudo-coherent complexes are exactly those with vanishing cohomology above m and finitely generated cohomology in degree m
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the base case of the induction.

standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness of cohomology in the top nonvanishing degree characterises pseudo-coherence one degree at a time
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides finiteness of the top cohomology module after localisation.

standard_prerequisites.name: Cone lemma for pseudo-coherence in a distinguished triangle
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Lemma \ref{lemma-cone-pseudo-coherent}, cited at proof lines 16439-16440 and 16443-16444
standard_prerequisites.use: Keeps the cone m-pseudo-coherent after localisation and finishes the induction.

core_obligations: Record that localisation is exact, so the localised cohomology is the cohomology of the localised complex (proof lines 16414-16418).
Let n be the largest degree with nonvanishing cohomology after some localisation and show that the complex has no cohomology above n (proof lines 16419-16423).
Settle the base case where n is below m using the characterisation of m-pseudo-coherence (proof lines 16424-16425).
Show that the cohomology in degree n is finite over the ring by the cover lemma, and choose a surjection from a finite free module, lifted to a map of complexes (proof lines 16426-16435).

Check that the cone has vanishing cohomology in degrees at least n and is m-pseudo-coherent after localisation, apply the induction hypothesis, and conclude by the cone lemma (proof lines 16436-16445).
proof_roadmap: Set up the induction and the top degree (proof lines 16414-16425).
Produce the finite free approximation in the top degree (proof lines 16426-16435).
Apply induction to the cone and conclude (proof lines 16436-16445).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that pseudo-coherence of a complex can be checked after localising at finitely many elements generating the unit ideal. The proof is an induction on the difference between the highest degree in which cohomology can be nonzero and the bounding degree m: the exactness of localisation identifies the localised cohomology with the cohomology of the localised complex, finiteness of the localised cohomology in the top degree plus the cover lemma gives finiteness of that cohomology module over the ring, and a surjection from a finite free module together with projectivity produces a map to the complex whose cone vanishes in high degrees and whose localisations remain m-pseudo-coherent by the cone lemma, so the induction applies and the cone lemma finishes the argument.
